body.x: WiseJet Co., Ltd. (CEO Chul Soon Park) captured the spotlight at CES 2025 from January 7–10 in Las Vegas. With a bold vision of replacing all electronic cables with wireless technology, the company unveiled its groundbreaking innovations at a dedicated booth in the Las Vegas Convention Center’s South Hall 3.

WiseJet’s centerpiece innovation, the Wireless CMOS Solution, is based on 60GHz high-speed wireless communication technology, pushing the boundaries of ultra-fast, high-definition data transmission. The XR-JET chip leads the showcase, capable of transmitting 8K/60Hz ultra-high-definition video over a 10-meter range with latency below 1 millisecond. Supporting data speeds of 10Gbps per lane, the chip has the potential to replace traditional cables in ultra-slim TVs, AR/VR, robotics, and medical devices.

CEO Chul Soon Park emphasized the company’s ambition: "We aim to remove all cables from electronic devices.” He highlighted WiseJet’s capabilities: "Our technology surpasses existing wireless standards like Wi-Fi, minimizing data loss and latency through uncompressed transmission.”

WiseJet’s booth has been a hub of activity, drawing visitors eager to witness its 8K/60Hz video transmission demos and proximity-based wireless data and power transfer solutions. The company’s beamforming technology, which enables data to bypass obstacles seamlessly, has particularly wowed audiences, demonstrating how it eliminates the need for HDMI and USB connectors in ultra-slim TVs.

body.cap: A variety of chips showcased at WiseJet’s CES 2025 booth | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In addition to long-range wireless solutions, WiseJet introduced its short-distance connectors, capable of working from 1mm to several centimeters. These connectors support various applications, from displays and VR/AR devices to camera inspection equipment, offering the industry a full-package wireless solution.

The company’s high-speed, high-definition data transfer solutions are poised to play a pivotal role in sectors like robotics, autonomous vehicles, medical devices, and digital signage. “WiseJet technology is perfectly aligned to meet the demands of the rapidly growing high-speed wireless communication market,” said Park.

Currently, WiseJet is collaborating with domestic and international clients on proof-of-concept (PoC) projects, solidifying its technological credentials. At CES 2025, visitors will experience firsthand how the company is reshaping the future of electronics with its cable-free innovations.
The industry eagerly anticipates WiseJet’s solutions' transformative impact, and CES 2025 will serve as a launchpad for its vision of a cable-free world.

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
